To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a duplicated goosecoid gene, GSX (goosecoid-related homeobox) is expressed in the chick embryo during gastrulation, and later in the neural plate, and (2) the two goosecoid proteins are functionally redundant during the transition from primitive streak to neural plate.
GSX is expressed during neurulation in chick embryo, that it has a homeobox similar, but not identical to GSC, and that the GSX expression domain segregates from the GSC domain during neurulation.
a duplicated basic goosecode identity is required for the generation of the chordate neural tube.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the vertebrate nervous system and its development.
the role of a duplicated basic Hox identity in the generation of a vertebrate neural plate.

the evolution of the basic plan for the development of the chordate nervous system, and we propose that a duplicated basic plan is the key for the evolution of a chordate body plan, with the posterior and anterior parts of the primitive streak being respectively the source of the chordate neural tube and the chordate notochord.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of the GSX and GSC genes in the primitive streak and pre-chordal region is correlated with the induction of gastrulation, while expression of the GSXD gene in the anterior primitive streak and neural plate is correlated with neurulation.
the two GSX genes are involved in the generation of the neural plate in a way that is not yet clear.

the two goosecoid-related genes, GSC and GSX, are differentially expressed during gastrulation and neurulation in chick, and that the two genes have distinct functions in the induction of the two processes, gastrulation and neurulaton.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two goosecoid-like genes, GSX and GSC, are involved in the generation of a vertebrate nervous system, but that they have different roles.

the two genes have similar functions in the primitive streak and that the expression domains of the genes are segregated to allow them to have separate roles in the gastrulating and neurulating parts of the primitive streak.
the two GSX and GSC genes are expressed in the same region of the primitive streak at the onset of gastrulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a duplicated basic goosecoidean identity, expressed in two different domains during the transition from the primitive streak to the neural plate, is a prerequisite for the generation of the chordate nervous system.
GSX is a bona fide goosecoid gene that is involved in gastrulation and neurulation in chicken embryos.
a duplication of a single gene can be sufficient to generate a new developmental function in a new embryological structure, the neural tube, which is a major evolutionary innovation in chordates.
